q-95261.name: Question 1
q-95261.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $4\times 3$ matrix $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

II. The singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]$ are non-negative.

III. Any $3\times 4$ matrix $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.
q-95261.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Since $A$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $3\times 4$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $3\times 3$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{3\times 4}\times {A}_{4\times 3}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{3\times 3}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is true. All singular values of any matrix are non-negative.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is a $3\times 4$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $4\times 4$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{4\times 3}\times {A}_{3\times 4}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{4\times 4}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

q-95362.name: Question 6
q-95362.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
q-95362.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (8-\lambda )(2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =8,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{8} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-94773.name: Question 7
q-94773.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
q-94773.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(8-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ 16-2\lambda -8\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -10) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =10,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{10} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=0\end{aligned}

q-95354.name: Question 13
q-95354.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
q-95354.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1-\lambda  & 0\end{aligned}|+(1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )[(2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-1)] & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1-1) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -3) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{3} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

ATA=[34]T[34]=[34][34]=[9121216]
